requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080 through node1's forwarding
requirements.summary: Bidirectional socat TCP/8080 connections succeed both before restarts (cmd-55da6530e9fc446e node2->node3, cmd-7380ddbbfa6d4fab node3->node2) and after the full restart cycle (cmd-b48e1317868e4b66, cmd-41f233638e0541b4), with data echoed correctly in both directions. Required opening the hosts' own firewalld port 8080 (cmd-5da6c27cd47344e8, cmd-2784a1097b5540a1) in addition to the node1 nftables accept rule.

requirements.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 traffic passing between node2 and node3
requirements.summary: An nftables forward-hook rule 'tcp dport 23 reject with tcp reset' is installed on node1 (cmd-48d90827990e45a7). Connection attempts to port 23 in both directions return 'Connection refused' both before restarts (cmd-55da6530e9fc446e, cmd-7380ddbbfa6d4fab) and after the full restart cycle (cmd-b48e1317868e4b66, cmd-41f233638e0541b4).

requirements.requirement: Rest of the forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 is left untouched
requirements.summary: ICMP ping between node2 and node3 succeeds throughout with ttl=63 (confirming a single router hop through node1), both before the ACL was applied (cmd-c12f65890d8a4b10) and after restarts (cmd-7380ddbbfa6d4fab, cmd-b48e1317868e4b66, cmd-41f233638e0541b4). The transit_acl table's chain policy is accept and contains only the two explicit rules for ports 23 and 8080, so no other traffic is affected.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, before/after evidence: node2 and node3 reach each other on TCP 8080 through node1, node1 refuses TCP 23 with a TCP reset, and other forwarded traffic (ICMP) is unaffected by the ACL. The independently required node-restart protocol was also completed for all three nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot IDs confirmed both in the executor trace and the fixed global lifecycle snapshots, and full recovery of addressing, forwarding, the ACL, and end-to-end connectivity. Hygiene is generally good but two unnecessary or unresolved mutations were found: an unexplained change to node1's unrelated docker0 interface, and residual socat test listeners left running on node2/node3 after the task finished.
limitations: Evidence relies on socat-based test listeners rather than a persistent real service; while sufficient to demonstrate the ACL's effect, the test listeners were not part of a production service and were left running as residue.
The docker0 interface mutation on node1 (cmd-ef2a74ead1a04f8e) has no stated justification tied to the task; its final state after restart was not explicitly re-verified in the trace.

Because SONiC's own interfaces file only manages eth0, node1's addressing/ACL persistence depends entirely on the custom transit-acl.service; this was validated once across a single reboot, which is sufficient evidence for the observed restart but leaves less margin than a native OS-level persistence mechanism would.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to the task: static addressing on node1/node2/node3 transit interfaces, persistent routes, ip_forward sysctls, the nftables transit_acl table, a systemd unit to persist node1's config, and firewalld port openings on node2/node3 that were diagnosed as necessary for 8080 to actually work. Two items are unnecessary or unresolved: (1) cmd-ef2a74ead1a04f8e removed the IP from and brought down node1's unrelated docker0 interface without any evidence-supported connection to the transit ACL task; it was retained (no command restores it). (2) The socat TCP-LISTEN test servers started on node2/node3 for ports 8080/23/2222 (e.g. cmd-881e3e7a60e0480b, cmd-8dea938f11c64c46, cmd-91c6de74f3aa49d7, cmd-9dfd66bc93204c59) were left running as residual listening sockets after task completion, visible in the after_executor listening-sockets snapshot on both nodes; these were useful for demonstrating connectivity but were not cleaned up. Several other mutations (ip route flush cache, ip neigh flush all, pkill socat, dhcp/lease checks) were bounded, low-risk diagnostic actions during troubleshooting of an intermittent 'No route to host' issue and did not leave meaningful residue.
